title_en: The Chocolates Left in the Taxi
note_en: 要不是… introduces an unreal condition, "if it weren't for …": 要不是这箱巧克力，他们俩说不定一辈子都不会重新联系上 "if it hadn't been for that box of chocolates, the two of them might never have gotten back in touch." Chinese has no special verb forms for counterfactuals; 要不是 alone signals that the situation is contrary to fact, where English needs "hadn't been" and "might never have."
